commander: Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the Warped Eclipse
list_researched: branch b3-v1 (decklist_sha256 8ae03aea6a219b6766a6a0e49d1cd83f83c33a16d0bd42ab489ce7ea30e4b515, 36 staged swaps 2026-11-12/13, unplayed), compared against the sleeved v1.4.0 only where a swap's purpose matters
consensus: Heliod, the Radiant Dawn lists (6,607 on EDHREC; 590 self-tagged bracket 3) are wheel decks first: Windfall 78.8%, Day's Undoing 62.5%, Echo of Eons 33.6% and Jace's Archivist 35.8% at bracket 3, backed by cheap symmetric draw (Cut a Deal 59.7%, Howling Mine 55.3%, Words of Wisdom 54.4%, Temple Bell 52.2%) and billed by Psychosis Crawler 62.0% and Scrawling Crawler 58.5%. Approach of the Second Sun is in 48.1% of bracket-3 lists and is the one non-mill kill the archetype agrees on; Laboratory Maniac (32.9%) is the other. Interaction is six-ish counterspells led by Arcane Denial 67.5%, Unwind 44.9% and Rewind 37.1%, plus Swords 62.9% and Path 46.8%; commander protection is Lightning Greaves 31.9% and Swiftfoot Boots 19.0%, not spells. Smothering Tithe (46.8%) is the Game Changer bracket-3 lists keep; Rhystic Study (16.3%) and Mystical Tutor (8.6%) are minority keeps. The branch's engine (X-draws discounted by Heliod, two draw-doublers, three-card Tithe infinites, a spell-based protection suite for Approach) is a sub-10% build on every one of its distinguishing cards; nothing fetched argues it is wrong, only that nobody else is measuring it.

findings.claim: The archetype's forced-draw engine is WHEELS, and the branch runs none. Windfall 78.8% (465/590), Day's Undoing 62.5%, Echo of Eons 33.6%, Wheel and Deal 25.6%, Time Reversal 23.1% on the bracket-3 page; Windfall is 87.0% on the Wheels theme (645 decks). None was ever in v1.4.0, so this is not a staged cut but an unexamined gap. A wheel is the largest single opponent-draw event in the identity (7 per opponent at 3 mana: 21 Heliod discount, 7 Scrawling life each, and 14-28 of your own draws under one or two doublers). The tension is real and the pilot must choose: Windfall and Day's Undoing discard the Approach in hand, and Day's Undoing ends your turn; both are compatible only with the top-of-library Approach plan (Mystical/Personal Tutor, Scroll Rack, Mystic Sanctuary) and hostile to the Solve-the-Equation-to-hand plan.

The cheapest consensus symmetric draw the branch lacks and never cut is Words of Wisdom (54.4% at bracket 3; {1}{U} instant: you draw two, each other player draws one). It is the only card above 50% on the bracket-3 page that is in identity, not a Game Changer, not excluded by a pilot rule, not staged out, and not already in the 99. Unwind (44.9%) and Rewind (37.1%) are the consensus counterspells the branch does not run; both untap lands, which under Heliod's discount is the same as free interaction. Everything else above 35% that the branch lacks was either cut on purpose with a stated why (Cut a Deal, Kwain, Kami of the Crescent Moon, Lore Broker, Temple Bell, Skyscribing, Reliquary Tower, Thought Vessel, Decanter of Endless Water, Mystic Remora) or is excluded by rule (Laboratory Maniac 32.9%; Hullbreaker Horror 37.0%, see the infinite finding).

The branch's Approach package is deeper than any measured bracket-3 list, and its protection shape matches the consensus where the consensus has one. Approach itself is 48.1% at bracket 3. Of the branch's finders and protectors the bracket-3 page lists Mystic Sanctuary 28.6%, Teferi, Time Raveler 20.7%, Solve the Equation 19.5%, Silence 15.8%, Mystical Tutor 8.6%; Scroll Rack, Sensei's Divining Top, Personal Tutor, Long-Term Plans, Dig Through Time, Pact of Negation and Grand Abolisher fall below the page's listing cutoff. Commander Spellbook's recorded Approach lines in the branch (Mystical Tutor 553-2856, Scroll Rack 553-1271, Personal Tutor 553-2674, Solve the Equation 553-7164, Venser 553-3634) state the prerequisites the pilot must meet: the Scroll Rack line needs 'at least eight cards in hand' and 13 generic plus WW; the Mystical Tutor line needs 'a way to draw a card' and 12 generic, WW, U. Heliod's discount pays only the generic part, which is why Vision Skeins (six opponent draws) before Approach matters. Consensus protection the branch does NOT run: Lightning Greaves 31.9%, Swiftfoot Boots 19.0%, Dawn's Truce 20.5% on the Wheels page. Grand Abolisher is in identity and legal but unlisted at bracket 3.

Game Changers: the branch's three (Mystical Tutor, Rhystic Study, Smothering Tithe) are exactly the three the commander's bracket-3 players keep, in the consensus's order (Tithe 46.8%, Rhystic 16.3%, Mystical 8.6%). Farewell was ADDED to the Game Changers list on 2026-02-09 (WotC: 'Farewell is a large reset to a lot of what has happened in the game before it'); it sits at 11.7% on the bracket-3 page from before that change and must not be the branch's next sweeper. The corpus's game_changer flag already carries Farewell. Every other GC the sleeved list ran (Consecrated Sphinx, Cyclonic Rift, Enlightened Tutor, Fierce Guardianship, Teferi's Protection) is staged out, so the branch holds at three; Narset, Parter of Veils and Drannith Magistrate are the in-identity GCs a future add could stumble on. Mana Drain, Force of Negation, Pact of Negation, Teferi, Time Raveler, Grand Abolisher, Sensei's Divining Top and Scroll Rack are NOT Game Changers as of the 2026-02-09 list.

Two-card infinites: none in the branch, by two independent checks, and three popular consensus cards would create one. The bench's Spellbook snapshot (114,443 variants, 2026-10-10) finds zero two-card infinites in the branch and two three-card ones (Bard, King of Dale + Gleaming Splendor + Smothering Tithe, id 4682-7824-7890; Faerie Mastermind + Mirrormade + Smothering Tithe, id 184-2210-4682). Live Spellbook queries on 2026-11-21: Mathemagics has no recorded line of three cards or fewer; Folio of Fancies has one two-card line and its partner (Peer into the Abyss) is black; Heliod himself has one two-card infinite, with Ancestral Statue (colourless, Commander-legal, in identity: do not add it). The repo's near-miss list names the consensus cards that would complete a two-card infinite with cards already in the branch: Hullbreaker Horror (37.0% at bracket 3) with Sol Ring; Dramatic Reversal (5.8%) and Narset's Reversal with Isochron Scepter; Tidespout Tyrant with Sol Ring; Heliod, Sun-Crowned with Walking Ballista. Displacer Kitten + Teferi, Time Raveler + Sol Ring is a three-card infinite the branch is one card from.

The forced-draw kill's arithmetic, derived here from oracle text (no fetched source states it; status 'needs a stack scenario' for the doubling interaction). Psychosis Crawler drains each opponent 1 per card YOU draw, so three opponents at 40 need 40 of your draws; Teferi's Ageless Insight and Bard, King of Dale each replace a non-draw-step draw with two, so one doubler needs 20 draw events and both need 10. Mathemagics targeting yourself at X=4 (10 mana before discount) draws 16, i.e. 32 under one doubler and 64 under both; X=3 draws 8 and does not kill under one doubler. Blue Sun's Zenith or Stroke of Genius at X=20 kills under one doubler. Scrawling Crawler drains per OPPONENT draw, so Prosperity X=N adds N per opponent and 3N of Heliod discount for the next spell; with both Crawlers and one doubler, Prosperity X=14 kills (14 + 28). Forced Fruition adds 7 Scrawling life and 7 discount per opponent spell but never kills alone. The line therefore rests on one five-mana artifact creature (Psychosis Crawler, the kill-on-sight card in the 2023 articles too) and two doublers; the sleeved list's Alhammarret's Archive-class redundancy (colourless, legal, not in the 99) is the obvious third doubler, and Finale of Revelation (44.0% on the Wheels page) is the consensus's big self-draw.

findings.claim: Group-hug payoffs and fort: the branch matches the consensus on the punishers and the fort and is alone on the doublers. Psychosis Crawler 62.0%, Scrawling Crawler 58.5%, Faerie Mastermind 43.7%, Smothering Tithe 46.8%, Dictate of Kruphix 34.1%, Forced Fruition 34.1%, Howling Mine 55.3%, Font of Mythos 23.4%, Propaganda 37.0%, Ghostly Prison 31.5% are all in the branch. Sphere of Safety 6.6%, Teferi's Ageless Insight 9.3%, Gleaming Splendor 6.8%, Mirrormade 8.0%, Mathemagics 8.8%, Folio of Fancies 14.4%, Leyline of Anticipation 5.9%, Walking Ballista 12.0% are minority; Bard, King of Dale, The Second Doctor, Isochron Scepter, Soul-Guide Lantern, Winds of Abandon, Archmage's Charm, Venser, Flawless Maneuver, Guardian of Faith and Karametra's Blessing are below the bracket-3 page's listing cutoff. The branch's no-maximum-hand-size coverage is Folio of Fancies and The Second Doctor only, after cutting Reliquary Tower (65.3%), Thought Vessel (58.8%) and Decanter (39.3%) on purpose; both survivors are permanents a sweeper or Austere Command's own artifact mode removes.

Interaction counts. The EDHREC group-hug average deck (239 decks) carries six counterspells (An Offer You Can't Refuse, Arcane Denial, Counterspell, Dovin's Veto, Rewind, Unwind), three spot removal (Oblation, Path, Swords), one sweeper-class card (none; Finale of Glory is a token maker), Teferi, Time Raveler, and no creature-protection spells. The branch carries seven hard counters (Offer, Arcane Denial, Archmage's Charm, Counterspell, Dovin's Veto, Force of Negation, Pact of Negation) plus Venser, three spot removal (Swords, Path, Winds of Abandon), two sweepers (Supreme Verdict, Austere Command) plus Winds overloaded, seven protection pieces (Silence, Teferi, Flawless Maneuver, Guardian of Faith, Karametra's Blessing, Greater Auramancy, Spellskite) and a four-piece fort. It is more interactive than the consensus on every axis except equipment-based commander protection.

known_failure_modes: Losing the commander to removal with no protection on it; the 2023 CoolStuffInc test game lost Heliod to enchantment removal ('Enchantment removal. On my commander.') and recommends Greaves/Boots. The pilot's log (001, 003) records the same shape.

Draw-hate shuts the whole engine: Narset, Parter of Veils ('Each opponent can't draw more than one card each turn') and Notion Thief redirect or cap the draws the discount, the Crawlers and the Tithe all key on; both are Game Changers and bracket-3 legal for opponents at the three-GC limit.

Feeding the strongest opponent: both 2023 articles warn that symmetric draw accelerates whoever can use the cards; the CoolStuffInc author's rule is to aim draw at players missing land drops or tapped out.
Table attention and long turns: Cardsrealm notes wheel decks 'attract attention' and offers 'You're drawing cards thanks to me' as the stall; CoolStuffInc notes the turns were 'messy and very long'.

Decking yourself: under two doublers a single Mathemagics or Zenith can draw more cards than the library holds; the kill must be sized to the library as well as to 40 life (derived here, not sourced).
Wheels (if adopted) discard an Approach in hand; Day's Undoing also ends your turn and so cannot be followed by a kill the same turn.
contested: Wheels vs X-draws: the consensus engine is Windfall/Day's Undoing/Echo of Eons; the pilot's thesis is every-player X draws (Prosperity, Fascination, Folio, Mathemagics). Nothing fetched measures which produces more Heliod discount per mana; the branch's own goldfish is the only instrument that could.

Laboratory Maniac (32.9% at bracket 3) and Jace, Wielder of Mysteries (10.9%) are the archetype's second kill; the pilot excludes mill/Lab Man by rule. Both 2023 articles call the Lab Man plan risky or 'cEDH'.
Rhystic Study vs Mystic Remora at bracket 3: Remora 24.1% edges Rhystic 16.3% on the self-tagged page; the branch keeps Rhystic (a GC) and cut Remora for Bard.

Protection shape: consensus protects the commander with equipment (Greaves 31.9%, Boots 19.0%); the branch protects with spells (Flawless Maneuver, Guardian of Faith, Karametra's Blessing, Greater Auramancy, Spellskite). The Draftsim and WotC pages confirm none of the branch's choices is a Game Changer, so the difference is taste, not bracket.

gaps: EDHREC's bracket pages are SELF-TAGGED: 590 of 6,607 decks carry a bracket; the figures describe what players calling themselves bracket 3 run, not a measured bracket.

EDHREC lists only cards above an inclusion cutoff; Grand Abolisher, Pact of Negation, Scroll Rack, Sensei's Divining Top, Personal Tutor, Long-Term Plans, Dig Through Time and Bard, King of Dale do not appear on the bracket-3 page, so their rate there is 'below the cutoff', not a number.

No written primer for a bracket-3 Heliod built on Approach plus discounted X-draws was found; the two articles are 2023 wheels builds, pre-brackets. Reddit is blocked to this agent; Moxfield's API returned 403; a DeckCheck page that reportedly named Notion Thief and Narset as the hosers did not render and is not cited.
Commander Spellbook's find-my-combos endpoint needs a POST; the whole-list two-card check is the bench's 2026-10-10 snapshot plus three targeted live queries (Heliod, Mathemagics, Folio).
The forced-draw kill arithmetic and the Insight + Bard 'four cards' claim are derived from oracle text here, not sourced; the doubling interaction needs a stack scenario before anyone writes 'four'.
No fetched source states inclusion for Approach-specific protection (Silence, Grand Abolisher, Pact) WITHIN Approach decks; EDHREC's card-page JSON returned site-wide category figures only.
The bracket-3 Game Changer allowance was not restated in the two WotC pages fetched; the bench's bracket_report (floor 3 on three GCs) is the artifact to trust for the count.
